reviews.review: I bought this game thinking that it would be a pretty short and silly game, but it has a pretty surprising amount of depth. There are upgrades to make to your base, physical fitness trees, survival trees, obscure things to unlock and access around the world. There is a wide array of weapons to discover and use. There is a pretty fun sense of humor behind it all. The downside is that there is a LOT of RNG. Safes, chests, boxes all spawn random things, and when there is one specific obscure item you need for your quest it can be really tedious to try to get it. I am not a fan of how the level 2 J-Lab pass randomly spawns, it seems like that one should permanently unlock. I would also say to not be too hung up on adjusting the difficulty level to how you like to play. I would also note that I don't use mods, so haven't been involved in the mod with malicious code issue that others have addressed.

Just beat the game an hour ago; wanted to give some thoughts on it. I also want to clarify that I'm a [b]vanilla [/b]player and have never modded or downloaded anything from the workshop. I only recently became aware of some issues with the developers and their…handling…of the malicious code situation. I'm unable to comment on all that; I'm sure others have already shared more on that matter.

The game itself is solid, with smooth performance all around and no crashes on my end. You play as a duck trying to escape the planet, making allies along the way who have the same idea and work together (doing quests) to figure that out. You're also killing [b]A LOT [/b]of other ducks who don't tolerate your existence.

It [i]is[/i] also a grindy game; it became that way after ~40 hours in. This is a single-player, PVE extraction shooter; I guess that is to be expected at some point. Loot is RNG; it doesn't matter so much in the beginning but can be a bit frustrating at times if you're missing a specific drop needed to upgrade your gear or turn in for the quest. To counter some of that, you do have unique mechanics such as teleportation, map shortcuts, and permanent key unlocks. Dying is not really a big deal; it gives you one chance to grab your corpse in the next run. If that becomes too frustrating, there's always cheesier methods (restoring your previous autosave), if that's your drift.

Speaking of the progression aspect, this game really nailed it out of the park. It's very laid back; I can take as much time as needed to upgrade my hideout, storage, and permanent bonuses to the character and am rewarded for all of it. There is a HUGE amount of items to collect, hoard, and use up as you naturally become stronger and able to take on entire maps. Don't get complacent; dying can happen quite quickly if you don't pick the battles. Running away is a completely valid strategy.

I'm sure there are QoL additions, such as item qualities, markers for the bosses, more stacking, etc., that should be added to the base game. Fishing could be a bit more fun. But honestly? The core gameloop and the gunplay/customization are what kept me going. I got plenty of enjoyment out of it, enough to 100% it achievement-wise. Maybe that's not such a bad outcome.

Overall, this is a game for those wanting a casual but quickly engaging experience; it definitely scratched an itch for me. I hope it continues to be successful and any negative lessons are learned by the dev team.
I find this game to be the perfect balance between fun, ability to customize and replayability.

Not recommended — not because of the game itself, but because of how malicious mod behavior is tolerated and enabled.
Within this game’s mod ecosystem, there exists severely unethical behavior that violates basic modding community norms.
A mod author secretly embedded a blacklist system into their mod.
When the game launches, it checks the player’s Steam ID, and if the ID is on the blacklist, the game is forcibly closed without any warning or notification.
This is not “author preference” — this is deliberate malicious code.
What makes it worse is how arbitrary the blacklist is:
Players have been added simply for politely reporting bugs, with no harassment or hostile language involved — merely because the author found them “annoying”.
After the source code was publicly exposed, the author:
Openly admitted the blacklist existed
Claimed they had done nothing wrong
Personally attacked critics
And members of their inner circle publicly insulted players and even threatened to upload malware mods in the future
All of this happened publicly and is well-documented.
The most disappointing part is the developer’s response.
In other communities (e.g. RimWorld), developers have directly intervened and removed malicious mods.
Here, however, players who contacted the devs found that:
The mod author was treated with excessive deference (addressed as a “respected teacher”)
The author reportedly received official merchandise gifts
The devs only made polite suggestions instead of taking action
While simultaneously telling the community that “the developer has requested the removal of malicious code”
This contradiction was later confirmed by the mod author themselves, who leaked the chat screenshots.
In short:
Buying this game also means accepting an ecosystem where
malicious mod behavior is tolerated and effectively protected.
If you care about:
Basic player rights
Mod transparency and safety
Developers genuinely standing with players
Then please think carefully before purchasing.
